_fix_efficacy_measured: MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. Ran the post-fix build_phantom_gdf/build_extended_gt against the live 4,746-feature student layer and the real canonical-review.csv in the project venv: at R=50 m (415 phantoms) the shipped tolerance of 1.0 m drops DROPPED=1; at 2.0 m still 1; only at 10.0 m does it drop 2. Identical pattern at R=75 m (594 phantoms). So the durable fix removes ONE of the TWO channel-duplicated rescues in the canonical Track-2 extended GT and leaves the other in place. Reason: the two canonical phantoms sit at 0.984 m and 6.783 m from their curator twins (they are cluster CENTROIDS of 2-3 cross-run review rows, so they are not at exactly 0.000 m). The 1 m tolerance catches the 0.984 m row by a margin of just 16 mm and misses the 6.783 m row entirely. Measured across all eight duplicate instances found in this sweep, the 1 m tolerance catches only the three exact-coincidence (0.000 m) cases plus that 0.984 m canonical row, and MISSES: 1.030 m (t0.3 cand 3107 — misses by 30 mm), 2.389 m (text-high cand 2903), 3.776 m (t0.3 cand 4660), 6.783 m (canonical row 148) and 16.781 m (text-min cand 4708). RECOMMENDATION FOR THE PI: the tolerance is calibrated to the exact-coincidence case described in the escalation, but the real instances are centroid-displaced. A tolerance around 10 m would catch all of them while remaining far below the ~20-25 m student digitisation jitter and the tens-of-metres spacing of genuinely distinct neighbouring mounds; the 1 m default additionally makes the one case it does catch fragile, since re-running build_canonical_gt.py with slightly different cluster membership could push that centroid past 1 m.

code_paths.notes: THE ENGINE OF THE DEFECT. build_phantom_gdf (L176) filters review rows to human_label=='mound' and gates by buffer_metres <= R (excluding the 200 m sentinel). build_extended_gt (L242) is a bare `pd.concat([s, p], ignore_index=True)` of student rows and phantom rows with NO spatial coincidence check whatsoever — confirmed by direct read of L242-262. Both student GT and review CSVs are CLI/kwarg-parameterised (input_paths recorded in summary.json metadata), so exposure is per-invocation, not intrinsic. Matching is per-map Hungarian one-to-one (compute_counts_at_r -> lib_advanced_metrics), so each surviving coincident pair costs exactly +1 unmatched GT point = +1 FN.

HIGHEST-VALUE CHECK — RESOLVED NEGATIVE. gather_reviews() (L72-98) builds its path list from ONLY review CSVs: the four CARRIED_RUNS 'results/{run}/human-review-multi-buffer.csv' plus the K3_RUNS x K3_SUBS 'human-review.csv' kits. It NEVER opens inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps-reviewed.geojson — the student layer is not an input to this script at all. Its de-dup (cluster(), L100-116) is a 20 m union-find over REVIEW POINTS ONLY, i.e. strictly phantom-vs-phantom. The reported ~600 duplicates it cleared were CROSS-RUN duplicate detections of the same feature (the same mound found by image + text-high + t0.3 = 3 review rows collapsing to 1). A phantom that duplicates a STUDENT point is structurally invisible to it. VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY against the emitted canonical-review.csv (773 rows): row candidate_id 72 (mound, buffer 50) sits 0.984 m from the cand-2397 curator point, and row candidate_id 148 (mound, buffer 50) sits 6.783 m from the cand-4264 curator point. Identical rows appear in auto-canonical-mounds.csv (740 rows). So build_canonical_gt.py does not merely fail to catch the twins — it PROPAGATES both of them into the canonical phantom set, at buffer_metres 50 so they gate in at every R >= 50 m. (The 0.984 m / 6.783 m offsets are the cluster CENTROIDS of the 2-3 cross-run review rows, which is why they are no longer exactly 0.000 m.)

Hard-codes STUDENT_GT = BASE_DIR/'inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps-reviewed.geojson' (L66, the LIVE post-duplication layer) and CANONICAL_REVIEW = results/deployment-oracle-2026-06-06/canonical-gt/canonical-review.csv (L70), with REVIEW_YESTERDAY = the header-only empty-yesterday-review.csv (L68). L332-336 read both and call build_phantom_gdf then build_extended_gt at BUFFER_M=50. So it DOES consume both channels with no de-dup. HOWEVER its output metric is STRUCTURALLY IMMUNE: lib_advanced_metrics.calculate_tile_classification (L1900-1965) classifies each tile by `has_mounds = len(refs_in_tile) > 0` — a boolean presence test. Adding a duplicate GT point inside a tile that already contains its twin cannot change has_mounds, so tile TP/TN/FP/FN and hence tile-MCC are bit-identical with or without the duplicates. Both twin pairs are separated by <= 6.8 m, far below tile size, so both duplicates land in already-positive tiles.

Imports build_extended_gt and build_phantom_gdf from the engine (L70-71) and calls them at L410-417 to build ext_gt_a / ext_gt_b. Student GT and both sides' review CSVs are CLI arguments (--student-gt, --review-yesterday-{a,b}, --review-today-{a,b}); it pre-gates yesterday by buffer_metres <= R at L406-407 to work around the latent over-promotion bug. No coincidence check. Materially mitigated in practice: the test statistic is a PAIRED per-tile difference and both arms are scored against the SAME extended GT, so a spurious GT point adds the same +1 FN to whichever arm(s) it affects on the same tile — the per-tile paired difference is invariant. Only the micro-averaged aggregate F1s move, by ~1e-4 each, and the observed delta by ~1e-5.

The S105 Track-2 driver. STUDENT_GT hard-coded to the LIVE layer (L66); CANONICAL_REVIEW passed as review_today for every cell; ensure_empty_yesterday() (L118-132) writes a header-only CSV as review_yesterday so all phantoms come from the canonical set ('matching how §4b ran: yesterday=0 today=773'). Delegates to the unmodified engine.run(), so it inherits build_extended_gt's missing coincidence check verbatim. This is the path that produced the canonical Track-2 numbers feeding the paper and the 55-map boards.

SIXTH EXPOSED CODE PATH — NOT in the escalation's list of five. Found by intersecting scripts that read student-mounds-55maps-reviewed.geojson with scripts that read a human-review CSV. It reimplements the pattern independently rather than importing it: load_inputs() (L105-135) builds student_slim and phantom_slim then `extended = gpd.GeoDataFrame(pd.concat([student_slim, phantom_slim], ignore_index=True))`, and matches with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment (L44, L99) — i.e. the same concat-then-one-to-one shape, same absent coincidence check. Its committed artefact is nevertheless SAFE-ERA (see artefacts): n_gt_total = 5216 = 4744 student + 472 phantoms, i.e. the 4,744 pre-duplication layer, and it has never been re-run.

Reads both channels and concatenates yesterday+today review mounds at L151, then drop_duplicates(subset='candidate_id') — an IDENTIFIER de-dup, not a spatial one, so it could never catch a cross-channel coincidence. But the concat is phantom-vs-phantom (review yesterday vs review today), not student-vs-phantom, and its reported statistic is a shell/lift curve over nearest-distance bands rather than one-to-one matched FN. Its committed summary.json records n_student_gt = 4744 (pre-duplication). Not a materially exposed path.

Five further scripts surfaced by the same intersection. All read the student layer AND a review CSV, and several concat yesterday+today review rows — but NONE builds a student+phantom extended GT scored by one-to-one Hungarian assignment. Every one of them reports NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR distance statistics (d_nearest_studentGT, nearest-GT distance distributions, shell rates, attractor pull). A nearest-distance metric is mathematically invariant to the addition of a coincident duplicate reference point: min over a set is unchanged by duplicating its argmin. Structurally immune, regardless of GT era.

Also in the intersection but they are review-KIT BUILDERS / the review UI, not scoring pipelines. They emit candidate manifests and crops for human adjudication; they do not publish an F1/recall artefact. review_candidates.py contains per-map Hungarian matching (L465) for candidate selection, not for a scored result. No scored artefact to verdict.

canonical_gt_finding: THE CANONICAL TRACK-2 EXTENDED GT IS EXPOSED, AND ITS DE-DUPLICATION CANNOT CATCH THIS DEFECT CLASS BY CONSTRUCTION. build_canonical_gt.py's gather_reviews() reads only review CSVs (four human-review-multi-buffer.csv from CARRIED_RUNS plus the k3-shell human-review.csv kits); inputs/vectors/references/student-mounds-55maps-reviewed.geojson is never opened. Its 20 m union-find de-dup is therefore strictly PHANTOM-vs-PHANTOM: the ~600 duplicates it cleared were the same real mound detected by several runs collapsing into one cluster. A phantom that duplicates a STUDENT-LAYER point is invisible to it. Verified empirically, not inferred: canonical-review.csv row candidate_id 72 (mound, buffer 50) lies 0.984 m from curator uuid manual-2026-05-03-K35-062-4-001 (cand 2397), and row candidate_id 148 (mound, buffer 50) lies 6.783 m from curator uuid manual-2026-05-03-K35-064-3-002 (cand 4264) — the sub-metre offsets are the cluster centroids of the 2-3 cross-run review rows the de-dup merged. So build_canonical_gt.py does not merely miss the twins; it launders them into a single authoritative-looking phantom each and PROPAGATES them. Consequently all eight canonical Track-2 cells (score_55maps_extended_gt_canonical.py, hard-coded to the live 4,746-feature layer, n_ref_student_only=4746 in every summary.json) score against an extended GT carrying exactly 2 spurious points at every R >= 50 m. The tile-MCC board is EXACTLY unaffected because tile classification is a boolean presence test. Recommended disposition: footnote, not rerun. A durable fix — a coincidence filter inside build_extended_gt — WAS landed mid-sweep by a concurrent session at commit 1de559119 (2026-08-04 08:56:53 +1000), but it is calibrated to 1.0 m and MEASURES AS ONLY HALF-EFFECTIVE ON THIS EXACT PATH: run against the live 4,746-feature layer and the real canonical-review.csv it drops 1 of the 2 duplicates at R=50 (and at R=75), because the canonical phantoms are cluster centroids sitting 0.984 m and 6.783 m from their curator twins. Raising dedup_tolerance_m to ~10 m drops both (verified empirically) and remains an order of magnitude below the ~20-25 m student digitisation jitter, so it cannot merge genuinely distinct neighbouring mounds. Until that tolerance is raised, the canonical Track-2 reference retains one spurious point at every R >= 50 m — halving, not eliminating, the ~+0.00017 bias.
